name: Soups, broths, and stocks (canned, dry-mix, bouillon, RTD carton)
native_basis_label: as consumed / ready-to-serve (reconstituted to serving strength; dry-mix and bouillon assessed as prepared, not as the concentrate)
scope_note: Canned soups, dry soup mixes, bouillon cubes and powders, and ready-to-drink carton stocks and broths, plant- or meat-based, including seafood-based bisques and chowders. Assessed on an as-consumed (reconstituted-to-serving) basis: a bouillon cube is evaluated as the prepared broth, not as the concentrated cube, because there is no legislated concentrate-to-serving ratio. Bone broth is certified separately under row bone-broth. Composite method identical to mixed meals. Principal components for anchor selection are the vegetables, the meat, poultry, fish or other seafood protein, the cereal or noodle, the pulses, and the dairy fraction of cream-style and cheese-based variants. TIN IS FORM-DEPENDENT ON THIS ROW: canned soup is a canned food and is verified against the canned-foods tin ML, while dry mix, bouillon and carton RTD have no tinplate contact and no instrument reaches them, so v1.2 publishes tin as a control with the canned-foods ML as a companion rather than as a row-wide ceiling. Formulation water is an input specification rather than a component anchor: packaged-drinking-water parametric values (Cap. 132V bottled water at 10 ug/kg lead, 10 total arsenic, 3 cadmium, 50 total chromium; EU 2020/2184; US 21 CFR 165.110; Health Canada) govern water sold as the sole daily hydration source and are not composite food ceilings, so they are not adopted here. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite limit from a water instrument. DAIRY IS A PRINCIPAL COMPONENT AND ITS CEILINGS ARE IMPORTED. v1.1 excluded dairy on the ground that it 'carries its own Category 24 milk ceilings at the ingredient stage'. That argument is not available, because this row applies the opposite rule to seafood: the seafood component is likewise governed at its own stage by the Category 6 seafood ceilings and its component maximum levels ARE imported into the ladder (fish lead 300, fish total mercury 500, seafood inorganic arsenic 100 and 50). No mass or characterizing test distinguishes the two. The composite convention admits a component when it is a principal (characterizing or major-mass) component of products within the row as scoped, and cream is a major-mass component of a bisque or chowder while cheese is the characterizing component of a macaroni-and-cheese or a cheese-sauced meal, exactly as the fish in a fish pie is. Dairy is therefore ADMITTED, and hk_cap132v_pb_milk_20 and hk_cap132v_pb_secondary-milk-products_20 (Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products, 20 ug/kg lead each) enter the lead component set, which moves the published lead ceiling from 50 to 20 ug/kg. On total mercury the corresponding rows hk_cap132v_thg_milk_10 and hk_cap132v_thg_secondary-milk-products_10 are admitted at 10 ug/kg and tie with the binding vegetable value, so the published mercury ceiling is unchanged. On cadmium, total arsenic, nickel and total chromium no credible regulator publishes a dairy row at all, which is stated here rather than left as a silence. Cap. 132V Note 10 scopes Secondary milk products to products that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, so neither Cap. 132V row directly regulates cream or cheese; the milk value is the nearest applicable sovereign anchor for the dairy component and is adopted by disclosed read-across, which is what every other component on this row does and what Method v2.0 prescribes for an unregulated exact cell. The alternative considered and rejected was narrowing the row to exclude cream-style and cheese-based products; that would contradict this row's own product examples, would strand chowder, bisque and macaroni-and-cheese formats with no certifiable home, and is a Step 0 taxonomy decision rather than a limit-setting one.
material: Multi-component composite food in four distinct physical forms that do not share a packaging pathway: canned soup in a tinplate or coated can; dry soup mix and bouillon cube or powder in a foil, laminate or paper wrap; and ready-to-drink stock or broth in an aseptic board carton, pouch or bottle. Composition is a vegetable fraction, a meat, poultry, fish or aquatic-invertebrate protein fraction, a cereal or noodle fraction, a pulse fraction, a dairy fraction in cream-style variants, salt and seasoning, and formulation water.
components: COMPONENT-LEVEL SAMPLING PLAN. The certified unit is the production lot, and the plan is form-dependent because this row's tin obligation is form-dependent. (1) PRIMARY UNIT: the product AS SERVED. A canned or carton lot is analysed as sold; a dry mix, bouillon cube or bouillon powder is reconstituted to the serving strength printed on the pack and analysed as the prepared broth, never as the concentrate, and the reconstitution ratio used is recorded on the certificate. A composite of not fewer than three retail units per lot, drawn across the run, for all eleven panel cells. (2) SEPARATELY SAMPLED FRACTIONS, required whenever a panel result on the as-served product is materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation: the vegetable fraction, the protein fraction, the cereal or noodle fraction, the pulse fraction, the dairy fraction, and the seasoning and salt fraction. (3) SEAFOOD REFLEX: on a bisque, chowder, fish stock or any seafood-containing formulation, the seafood fraction is retained for reflex methylmercury speciation and reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation, analysed whenever total mercury or total arsenic approaches the published ceiling. (4) PACKAGING, the escalation target for the tin and aluminium controls and the reason tin is a control rather than a row-wide ceiling on this row: the can body, lid and internal coating for the canned form; the foil, laminate or paper wrap of the bouillon cube and the dry-mix sachet; and the carton laminate, closure and pouch film for the ready-to-drink form. A canned lot is additionally verified against the canned-food tin maximum level named in the tin cell's companion set. (5) INGREDIENT WATER, which is the majority of this product by mass, verified on specification against the applicable national drinking-water standard and not used to re-derive the composite limit.
basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed in Cap 132V|as_sold
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a dietary food maximum level in a comparable as-consumed family (EU wet weight or product as placed on the market, FSANZ portion ordinarily consumed, Cap. 132V food as sold). The guard matters most on this row because a soup is mostly water: it stops a packaged-drinking-water parametric value, an animal-feed maximum, or a food-contact-material migration limit from silently anchoring a composite food cell, since those are different basis classes and are not comparable to a food-content ceiling. A cell whose named anchor falls outside the family fails the build instead of publishing a mixed-basis number. SCOPE OF WHAT THIS GUARD ACTUALLY DOES, corrected in v1.2: it refuses the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada drinking-water instruments, the EU 10/2011 specific migration limits, animal-feed maxima, and toy migration limits, because each carries a distinct basis string. It does NOT refuse the Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows, which share the single Cap. 132V basis string with that instrument's food rows and are therefore indistinguishable to a basis regex. Those rows are excluded by the stated ingredient-water determination and are named by id in each affected cell's companion set, not silently dropped.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; COMPOSITE — disclosed read-across from strictest applicable principal-component sovereign ML; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.label: the dairy component binds at 20 ug/kg (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, Milk and Secondary milk products), stricter than the fruiting-vegetable and preserved-tomato rows (50 each) that bound in v1.1 and stricter than the root/tuber vegetable (100), meat (100), cereal (200) and fish (300) components. Tightened from 100 to 50 in v1.1 on the Cap. 132V admission, and from 50 to 20 in v1.2 on the dairy ruling
Pb.substantiation: THE BINDING MOVED IN v1.2 BECAUSE THE DAIRY EXCLUSION DID NOT SURVIVE AUDIT, and it did not survive on this row in particular: the row's own component labels name bisque and chowder to justify the seafood anchor, and cream is a major-mass component of exactly those products, so calling dairy a minor formulation ingredient in cream-style variants contradicted the row's own text. The ruling and the rejected alternatives are stated in full in this row's scope_note; hk_cap132v_pb_milk_20 and hk_cap132v_pb_secondary-milk-products_20 are admitted and the ceiling is 20 ug/kg. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: a noodle soup (cereal lead 200) or a seafood chowder (fish 300) contains a component whose own sovereign ceiling is many times this composite ceiling and may measure above it; that does not loosen the ceiling, and a composite lot above 20 ug/kg lead is not certifiable on this row. The v1.1 ladder is retained and unchanged below the new binding: Cap. 132V sets lead at 50 ug/kg for fruiting vegetables (cucurbit and non-cucurbit) and for tomatoes preserved by heat treatment and hermetically sealed, and tomato soup is the flagship product of this row and is made from exactly that commodity. Two stricter Cap. 132V lead rows remain deliberately NOT adopted and are now equal to rather than stricter than the binding: cereal-based food (20 ug/kg) and ready-to-eat complementary food other than cereal-based (20 ug/kg), both scoped to persons under the age of 36 months; infant and toddler soups and purees route to HMTc Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule, and the Codex ready-to-eat meals for infants and young children ML (20 ug/kg) is dispositioned identically. Canned-vegetable (100) and leafy-vegetable (300) lead MLs are applicable but looser and are disclosed rather than adopted. BEVERAGE-COMMODITY RULING, applied once and consistently across every analyte on this row. Fruit and vegetable juices, nectars, rice-based drinks, and bottled and packaged waters are separately regulated ready-to-drink beverage commodities, consumed as the whole product, and they are NOT principal components of a prepared meal, soup, broth or stock. Where a formulation contains juice or juice concentrate it enters as a minor flavour, sweetener or acidulant fraction of a few percent, exactly like the cooking fat and the salt this row already dispositions as ingredient specifications rather than composite ceilings, and the vegetable commodity that a vegetable juice is pressed from is already in the ladder at its own maximum level (Cap. 132V fruiting vegetables and preserved tomatoes), so adopting the juice row as well would import the same commodity twice in a form this row does not sell. The rows dispositioned by this ruling, named by id so the choice is auditable: eu2024_ni_juice_250 (nickel 250, fruit/vegetable juices and nectars) and eu2024_ni_juice_listed_1000 (nickel 1000); fda2023_ias_apple_juice_10 (inorganic arsenic 10, apple juice), eu2023_ias_fruit_juice_20 (inorganic arsenic 20) and eu2023_ias_rice_drinks_30 (inorganic arsenic 30, non-alcoholic rice-based drinks); eu2023_pb_fruit_juice_other_30, hk_cap132v_pb_fruit-juices-other-than-fruit-juices-exclusively-from-b_30 and hk_cap132v_pb_grape-juice_40 (lead 30 to 40); and the packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values dispositioned in the row scope note. THE RULING IS TESTED BY ITS CONSEQUENCE: if a juice were a principal component, the US apple-juice inorganic-arsenic action level of 10 ug/kg would become the ceiling for an entire prepared meal, which no sovereign anywhere has set and which would be an occurrence-free but nonsensical import. Adopting the nickel juice row at 250 while declining the inorganic-arsenic juice row at 10 is the asymmetry this remediation exists to remove, so both are declined under one stated rule. v1.2 REMOVES juice, nectar and drink from this row's audit_exclude_scope so these rows now surface in the compiler's stricter-unselected scan and in the publication gate's W1 warnings, where they are dispositioned by this paragraph rather than suppressed by a regex. Nothing else stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant lead row below 20 ug/kg returns only drinking-water and bottled-water parametric values (5 to 10 ug/kg) and the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (10), both refused by this row's basis_guard. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.

tAs.label: Cap. 132V sets total arsenic at 500 ug/kg for vegetables, cereals other than rice, meat of animal and meat of poultry, covering every principal component of a soup or stock and stricter than the FSANZ cereal-grain ML (1000) that v1.0 selected. Total arsenic is published as a protective sovereign maximum level, not as a screen; the toxic inorganic fraction is separately and more strictly controlled on the iAs cell at 50 ug/kg.
tAs.substantiation: TOTAL ARSENIC IS PUBLISHED HERE AS A PROTECTIVE SOVEREIGN MAXIMUM LEVEL, NOT AS A SCREEN. v1.1 opened this substantiation with 'Total arsenic is a non-toxicological screen' while the cell emitted an ordinary numeric read-across with no screen flag, so the prose and the provenance disagreed about whether the published number was protective and any renderer that distinguishes the two would have contradicted the cell's own text. The disagreement is resolved in favour of what the cell in fact publishes: Cap. 132V regulates total arsenic as a per-commodity protective ceiling, 500 ug/kg is the strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic maximum level for the components of this row, and it is published as such. Total arsenic is one of the eight mandatory HMTc totals and is never satisfied by its species. The screen mechanism (`screen: true` with a screen_note) is used on this config only for total chromium, where the published value genuinely is not protective as a standalone total-element ceiling; it is not available on a component_read_across cell in this compiler in any case. The toxicologically dominant arsenic species, inorganic arsenic, is separately and far more strictly controlled on the iAs cell at 50 ug/kg (EU 2025/1891 cephalopods), and the species-below-total relation holds (iAs 50 <= tAs 500). v1.1 tightens the cell from 1000 to 500 ug/kg on the Cap. 132V per-commodity total-arsenic MLs, and the v1.0 claim that cereal grains carry the only credible total-arsenic component ML is withdrawn. Rice is absent from Cap. 132V's total-arsenic schedule because rice is regulated on inorganic arsenic; congee and rice soups are therefore controlled through the iAs cell, never by substituting a species for a total. The Cap. 132V edible-fats-and-oils total-arsenic ML (100 ug/kg) and the food-grade-salt ML (500) are not adopted: cooking fat and salt are minor formulation ingredients rather than characterizing components, they certify under HMTc Categories 30 and 34 in their own bases, and importing either would set a whole-soup ceiling from a material that is a small percentage of the product. Packaged-drinking-water total arsenic (10 ug/kg) is dispositioned in the row scope note as an ingredient-water specification. Nothing else stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant total-arsenic row below 500 ug/kg returns drinking-water and bottled-water parametric values (10) and the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (10), both refused by this row's basis_guard; and us_fda_21cfr73_73_520_tas_50 at 50, which is a colour-additive ingredient specification for soy leghemoglobin under 21 CFR 73.520, a purity specification for an additive as supplied rather than a contaminant ceiling for a food as sold, dispositioned in the same form as the edible-fats-and-oils and salt rows below. The stricter rung is adopted, the equal rungs are named, and the looser rungs are disclosed and not adopted. tHg.label: the vegetable total-mercury ML (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, 10 ug/kg) binds. v1.1 replaces the v1.0 seafood-only anchor of 500 ug/kg: Cap. 132V sets mercury MLs for the terrestrial components of a soup or stock (vegetables 10, rice/maize/wheat and their flours 20, meat of animal 50, meat of poultry 50, poultry eggs 50), and vegetables are a principal component of nearly every product in this row.
tHg.substantiation: The v1.0 statement that no credible regulator sets a mercury ML for terrestrial-meat or vegetable stock was true only while Hong Kong sat outside the credible-regulator set. Cap. 132V was admitted on 2026-08-17 and its mercury item (expressed as total mercury) sets 10 ug/kg for vegetables other than edible fungi, 20 for rice, maize and wheat and their flours, and 50 for meat of animal, meat of poultry and poultry eggs. The strictest applicable component moves this cell from 500 to 10 ug/kg and the false claim is corrected rather than preserved. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: a seafood-characterized soup (clam chowder, lobster bisque, fish stock) carries a component whose own sovereign ceiling is 500 ug/kg (EU 2023/915 fish; Cap. 132V aquatic animals other than fish, 500) and will frequently measure above this composite ceiling. That does not loosen the ceiling. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg); its only pathway in a soup is a seafood component, governed by the published total-mercury ceiling of 10 ug/kg on the tHg cell. Every one of them is an aquatic-animal instrument and every one is looser than this row's binding total-mercury ceiling of 10 ug/kg, so none can bind. v1.2 CORRECTS A COMPLETENESS CLAIM: v1.1 asserted that the only credible methylmercury MLs on the register were the Cap. 132V fish-species rows, in the same sentence whose instruments-checked list named US FDA CPG 540.600, so the record demonstrated that it had looked at the instrument and then mis-stated what it found. The determination itself is unaffected, since 1000 is far above the binding 10.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by closed-vessel acid digestion with ICP-MS or CV-AAS on the reconstituted as-served soup; reflex methylmercury speciation (species-specific isotope dilution GC-ICP-MS) only on a seafood-based soup whose total mercury approaches the total-mercury ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible regulator sets a methylmercury content limit for a composite soup, broth or stock; methylmercury MLs are scoped to individual fish species and to aquatic animals generally. MeHg is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), governed through the total-mercury cell at 10 ug/kg. EVIDENCE TEST, AND WHY THE TWO COMPOSITE ROWS OF THIS CATEGORY RESOLVE METHYLMERCURY DIFFERENTLY. hwang2022-home-meal-replacement-heavy-metals measured methylmercury directly in 480 Korean home-meal-replacement products and reported it BY MATRIX PHASE: detected in the non-fatty solid phase (mean 3.0, maximum 48.0 ug/kg) and the fatty solid phase, and NOT DETECTED in both the non-fatty liquid phase and the fatty liquid phase. A soup, broth or stock is the liquid phase, and a plated frozen dinner is the solid phase. That is why mixed-meals-prepared-foods holds methylmercury under mandatory analytical control (the species was measured in its matrix, so a not-material determination is not supportable there) while this row records a substantiated not-material determination with a reflex trigger. The asymmetry is evidence-driven and is recorded here rather than left to look like an inconsistency. Occurrence evidence is used only to test materiality, never to select a number (Method v2.0).

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin is a tinplate migration pathway confined to the canned form, and three of the four forms this row certifies are not canned foods. The subcategory as scoped covers canned soups, dry soup mixes, bouillon cubes and powders, and ready-to-drink carton stocks and broths; the canned-foods tin maximum level reaches only the first. v1.1 published that ML as a row-wide firm ceiling of 250 mg/kg while its own label conceded that dry-mix, bouillon and carton-RTD forms have no tin migration pathway, so the compiled record asserted a 250 mg/kg tin ceiling for a carton broth that no instrument sets and the publication gate counted it as a firm protective limit. v1.2 converts the cell to the control + companion_ml pattern the other two rows of this category already use (mixed-meals-prepared-foods and bone-broth), so the canned form is verified against the ML while no ceiling is asserted for the forms the instrument does not reach. A form-split cell was considered and is not available in this compiler. A CANNED soup is verified against the canned-foods tin ML, on which three credible regulators converge at 250 mg/kg (250000 ug/kg): Codex CXS 193 (canned foods), FSANZ Schedule 19 (all canned foods) and HK Cap. 132V (canned food other than canned beverages), so the figure is not a single-jurisdiction artefact. The Cap. 132V canned-beverage row (150 mg/kg) is stricter but is not adopted: a ready-to-drink carton stock is not a canned beverage and has no tinplate contact, and a canned soup is a canned food under every one of these instruments. Instruments checked for the non-canned forms: EU 2023/915 (tin appears only as canned-food and canned-beverage MLs), Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19, Cap. 132V, US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments; none sets a tin maximum level for a dry soup mix, a bouillon cube or a carton broth. THE STRICTEST APPLICABLE CANNED-FOOD TIN ML IS THE EU ROW AT 200 mg/kg, NOT THE 250 mg/kg FIGURE v1.1 NAMED. Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 sets tin at 200000 ug/kg (200 mg/kg) for canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned powdered products (eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000, basis product as placed on the market). It is stricter than the three rows v1.1 named as converging at 250 mg/kg (codex_cxs193_sn_canned_250000, aunz_sch19_sn_canned_250000, hk_cap132v_sn_canned-food-other-than-canned-beverages_250000), it is a credible-regulator maximum level in a basis this row accepts, and it was neither named nor dispositioned. This defect was found by hand during the v1.2 remediation and NOT by the compiler safety-net, because the soups row's audit_exclude_scope contained the term `beverage`, which matched the phrase 'canned beverages' inside the EU row's own scope string and suppressed it from every scan; the same class of regex self-defeat the v1.2 audit identified elsewhere. The term is removed. The canned form is verified against the EU value, and the EU instrument's own carve-out for canned dried and canned powdered products is independent confirmation that a tin maximum level does not reach a dry soup mix or a bouillon powder. Stricter still, and disclosed rather than adopted because they reach a different form: canned beverages at 100 mg/kg (eu2023_sn_canned_beverages_100000) and at 150 mg/kg (hk_cap132v_sn_canned-beverages_150000). Where a certified product is a canned drinkable broth presented as a beverage rather than a canned food, the canned-beverage value is the applicable one and the stricter of the two applicable rows governs; no single number is asserted across forms.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS, one determination per production lot, on the reconstituted as-served soup for dry-mix and bouillon forms and on the as-sold contents for canned and carton forms. A canned lot is verified against the canned-foods tin ML named in companion_ml. ESCALATION: any measurable tin on a dry-mix, bouillon or carton lot triggers packaging-source investigation (shared-line can or lid contact, tinned solder, foil or laminate liner, or a tin-bearing additive), with a confirmatory second lot before release.

Al.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium maximum level for a soup, stock or bouillon, or for any principal component of one. Instruments checked: EU 2023/915 and EU 2024/1987 (no aluminium entry), Codex CXS 193 (no aluminium entry), FSANZ Schedule 19 (aluminium appears only as infant-formula MLs of 500 and 1000 ug/kg, Category 1 scope), Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (no aluminium entry), and US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments (no aluminium ML). Aluminium reaches the credible register only in basis families that cannot anchor a food-content cell: drinking-water parametric values (EU 2020/2184 and US 21 CFR 165.110 at 200 ug/L, Health Canada at 2900 ug/L), food-contact-material specific migration limits (EU 10/2011), and toy migration limits. Aluminium-containing additive maxima exist only in non-credible-tier instruments and are additive-use levels, not contaminant ceilings. Aluminium is therefore a mandatory reported cell with no invented ceiling.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS on the reconstituted as-served soup, one determination per production lot, reported with no numeric pass/fail. Escalation: a result materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation triggers investigation of aluminium kettles, pans and contact surfaces, foil and laminate packaging including bouillon cube wrap, and any aluminium-containing additive, with a confirmatory second lot before release.

Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
